page.layout: One page of running text, set in one column, with a running head at the top left, a page number at the top right, and a small italic subtitle beneath the running head. Below the text are three worked number displays (division layouts) and a short example. No margin notes.

main_text.head: Quid est Divisio.
main_text.p: Divisio est numeratio, qua numerus dividitur per nūmerum[?], & habetur Quotus.

Sumit autem Divisio à sinistra initium. Numerus qui dividitur dicitur Dividendus,is qui dividit, dicitur Divisor, Tertius q[?] ex Divisione provenit, dicitur Quoriens seu Quotus, & scribitur versus dextrâ post semicirculum.
Quando Divisor Dividendo par est vel minor, ponitur primus sub primum, secundus sub secundum, & sic deinceps, à sinistra progrediendo ad dextram, hoc modo:
Cùm autem Divisor major est Dividendo, tum promovetur, hoc modo:
Si Divisor habet unam vel plures nullas eæ versus dextram in fine sub Dividendo ponuntur: Et quicquid supra o fuerit, est residuum, hoc modo:
main_text.head: Exemplum cum uno Divisore.

page.notes: The two-line division display and the worked example at the foot are reproduced as they appear; their spacing is approximate. The circled or bracketed digits "(4 3" and "(17" in the residue display are uncertain and marked [?]. The "q" before "ex" in "Tertius q ex Divisione" is a contracted form, read as q[?]. The macron over "nu" in "numerum" is uncertain. The subtitle "Quid est Divisio." is treated as a level 2 heading. Long s has been normalised to s throughout, as instructed, so "eft", "finistra" and similar forms appear as est, sinistra. The first letter of "sunt" in the example line is hard to read and may be a printed "f"-like long s; it is given as sunt.
